label: Phase 1 tank hits and raid pulses, scaled so gear separates
summary: One healer's share of a Phase 1 raid fight, scaled up until the strongest raid-ready healer covers about 80 percent of what comes in and the weakest about 60: a tank taking big melee hits, raid-wide damage in regular pulses, and four more raid members to look after, with the healer taking its share of the raid-wide damage.
notes: A healing sim ranks gear under a stated incoming-damage profile. It never says one healer class beats another, and every healer number the site publishes names this profile. No client table states a creature's damage, so every figure below is a stated assumption, and this profile is a stand-in for Phase 1 that is NOT a named boss. It was first sized to an Onyxia-class boss, but at that size the raid-ready healers covered 80 to 97 percent of what came in, healing met the damage, and more healing power changed nothing, so gear tied. The retune rule (design/reviews/2026-10-08-heal-profile-retune.md) is: scale the tank hit size and the raid-wide pulse damage together, keeping their ratio and cadence, by the smallest multiplier at which the strongest raid-ready healer covers about 80 percent of the incoming damage, the weakest about 60, every bare set (no raid consumables) covers less than half, and mana is a live constraint (a bare set's mana runs out before the fight ends for every healer, and a raid set's for at least one). The multiplier chosen was 1.5 on 2026-10-08 and is 1.65 since 2026-11-01: client 1.60.1.70707 gave the Restoration druid Bloom and let heals over time crit (the client flags every trained heal over time PERIODIC_CAN_CRIT, and Blizzard's beta notes of 24 September say so for Rejuvenation), which took the druid to 91 percent at 1.5, and 1.65 is the smallest multiplier that brings every raid set back between about 60 and 85 percent (design/reviews/2026-11-01-sim-audit-round4/hybrids.md). It is 1.85 since 2026-11-02: round 7's engine fixes (Mana Spring stacking with Blessing of Wisdom, Healing Stream counted in the shaman's healing, Oath of Light, Water Shield on raid damage, casts pushed back by the pulses) took the Restoration shaman to 97 percent at 1.65, and 1.85 is the smallest multiplier that brings every raid set back between about 60 and 85 percent on the published gear (design/reviews/2026-11-02-sim-audit-round7/healers.md). The next retune (Phase 2 gear) follows the same rule. The figures are damage AFTER mitigation, because the fake raid has no armor or avoidance to roll. They are the share of the fight one healer is asked to cover, not the whole raid's incoming damage, and they stay the same for every spec and every gear set so the ranking compares gear and not fights.

tuning.reason: The tank hit and the raid pulse are the Onyxia-class figures first assumed (1,150 and 300) times one multiplier, set by the retune rule: 1.5 on 2026-10-08, 1.65 on 2026-11-01 once the client let heals over time crit, 1.85 on 2026-11-02 once the engine fixes of round 7 (Mana Spring stacking with Blessing of Wisdom, Healing Stream counted, Oath of Light, Water Shield on raid damage) took the strongest raid set to 97 percent. The multiplier is a tuning, not a measured boss, so the two answers are its bounds: /tiers/healer orders two healers only when the order holds, and the gap is beyond the error, at both.

tank.reason: A raid tank has about 9,500 health in Phase 1 gear with raid buffs. The hit is a stand-in sized by the retune rule, not a boss's: 1.85 times the 1,150 an Onyxia-class boss was first assumed to land on a mitigated tank, which is the smallest scale at which the five healers' raid-ready sets cover between about 60 and 85 percent of the incoming damage and bare sets less than half. With misses, dodges and parries averaged in one hit lands about every 3.3 seconds, about 645 damage a second; each hit rolls 25 percent either side.

members.reason: A raid member that is not the tank has about 5,000 health: a plate or mail wearer sits above it and a cloth wearer below.

pulse.reason: Raid-wide damage in regular pulses (a breath, a wing buffet, a periodic shadow bolt volley): every five seconds three of the five members of the healer's group, the healer among them, take 555, about 333 damage a second spread over the group the healer stands in. The healer is one of the five because raid-wide damage does not skip the player casting the heals; until round 6 (design/reviews/2026-11-02-sim-audit-round6/healers.md) it landed only on the four others, so every group heal put a fifth of its healing on a healer who was never hurt. The total is unchanged: three members a pulse, now chosen from five. Scaled by the same 1.85 as the tank hit, so the tank-to-raid ratio and the cadence are what they were.
